data.title: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) partner, raptor, binds the mTOR substrates p70 S6 kinase and 4E-BP1 through their TOR signaling (TOS) motif
data.authors: Nojima H; Yonezawa K et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Raptor binds mTOR substrates via their TOS motifs, acting as the substrate-presenting scaffold of mTORC1.
data.abstract_excerpt: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) controls multiple cellular functions in response to amino acids and growth factors, in part by regulating the phosphorylation of p70 S6 kinase (p70S6k) and eukaryotic initiation factor 4E-binding protein 1 (4E-BP1). Raptor (regulatory associated protein of mTOR) is a recently identified mTOR binding partner that also binds p70S6k and 4E-BP1 and is essential for TOR signaling in vivo.

extracted_findings.effect: Raptor binds the mTOR substrates p70 S6K and 4E-BP1 through their TOR-signaling (TOS) motif
